notes_for_us: The count field holds "50 stages" but nothing in the handoff expresses that a stage is a unit of structure rather than a quantity of platforms. A fifty-stage obby is fifty segments each ending in a checkpoint, and that repetition is the whole build - segments would express it, but the rule says segments is for distinct spaces the user named, and these fifty are neither distinct nor named.

layout-intake tells me to offer the decomposed alternative when extent and detail cannot both be honoured, and to record the deferral in notes. It does not say whether to route P4 while offering it. I stayed on P6 alone and put the offer in a question, so a downstream reader sees one course; a lane that emitted P4 as well would look very different on the same prompt.

Three words with a number in them produced a four-question record, which feels right, but the shape question is genuinely open: Tower of Hell is the most famous fifty-stage-ish obby on the platform and it is a tower, so course-flat as the genre default may be the wrong prior for a stage-counted prompt.

notes_for_us: The scale table contradicts itself on this exact prompt: Room is described as typical of "escape room, single arena" and Block as typical of "most arenas, courses, courts, lobbies". A single arena is the example given for both bands. I took Block because a large roaming boss and ranged weapons need distance, but the table cannot be read to decide it.

The prompt's central request - generate one detailed creature mesh from a description - has no field anywhere in the handoff. It is not layout, not theme, not a constraint on the space, and not mechanics. I carried it as free text in image_prompt, where a segmenter looking for map geometry will most likely ignore it.

Action's genre note says a flat arena is perfectly valid and verticality is often wrongly assumed mandatory, which is useful, but the Boss Raid preset then ships destructible-cluster and hazard-kill unasked. This is the clearest case I hit of a run that ends with no place: the boss dies where it stands. Step 4 says the run needs somewhere to end and F6 fails a map with no reachable objective, so it is worth stating explicitly that a boss arena satisfies F6 through the boss rather than through a zone.

The three stacked UI buttons are positioned precisely (top right, then under, then under) and that detail is pure UI, but it is also the only structure the prompt gives to the customization system. It survived only as prose in mechanics.

Nothing in the handoff says whether ten maps means ten renders. P4 says separate maps; the count lives on teleporter-link; the two are not connected, so a downstream reader has to notice both to get ten.

notes_for_us: Nothing in the handoff holds in-world text. The whole point of this prompt is a specific name on a specific sign, misspelling included, and the only place it survives is inside a landmark-focal sentence and a build_rule constraint. A text-on-geometry option would have taken it cleanly.

Roleplay lists interior-single in its typical shapes but every preset in the genre uses a settlement or a runway, so the one-building case has no preset. Morph Roleplay with a swapped shape works, but an Indoor Roleplay preset - office, school, hospital, restaurant - would cover a large and obvious family.

The Roleplay-vs-Role-Sim boundary note was the decisive rule here and it was genuinely close: 'players can be working in a office' is a job, but there is no described task loop, so it stayed Roleplay. Borrowing trigger-task from Simulation was how I kept the working part without moving genre.

notes_for_us: This prompt starts with 'Add', and the skill has no additive mode. Every path through layout-intake emits a whole build, so an instruction to insert one room into an existing map comes out as a standalone casino map. Nothing in the files says what to do with a delta request, and I expect this shape of prompt is common once someone has a map they like.

'Purely decorative, not actually playable' looks like the SET trigger and is not one - SET is about walking, this is about interacting. The two readings are easy to confuse and stage B's phrasing does not distinguish decorative from unwalkable.

Two of the four picks came from the Indoor Venue preset rather than the prompt, on a one-sentence request. zone-graphics in particular is a performance-isolation feature nobody asked for; it happens to fit lit slot machines, but that is luck.

skill_gap.name: no additive request path
skill_gap.why: the prompt asks to add a lounge to an existing build and the handoff can only describe a complete map, so the relationship between the new room and the map it belongs to is unrepresentable
